text:
anna: Heads up — ran a head-split RoPE sweep across Llama-2-70B, Mistral-7B-v2, Mixtral-8x and Qwen-14B. Saw a subset of heads saturate and trigger perplexity spikes at long contexts (>8k) for the NTK/YARN variants. Posting quick notes and profiler snippets.

ben: Can you drop the profiler output? I suspect the kernel picker is flipping between fused matmul and a split-k kernel which would explain SM util drops.

anna: Pasted profiler excerpt below — look at end of batcher timeline, GPU SM drops, and increased KV cache misses. Short paste:
```
Batcher timeline (trace id 0x3f2):
- 0-200ms: enqueue/build
- 200-600ms: kernel A (fused_matmul_attn)
- 600-900ms: kernel B (split_k_attention)
metrics: p99_latency 180ms -> 260ms (+44%)
KV cache hit-rate 98% -> 87% at token 6k+
GPU SM util 78% -> 45% during tail windows
```

maya: Which model showed the worst behavior? Mixtral or Llama?

anna: Mixtral-8x exhibited the clearest head-saturation when rotary_scale > 1.2 in the NTK variant. Linear RoPE kept stable. Measured ppl delta: Mixtral NTK +1.8 ppl after 6k tokens vs linear. Mistral had milder effect, Qwen showed quality regressions when kv_evict windows were aggressive.

devon: Did you try the head-skip / head-prune heuristics or lowering the head cache window? Batcher might be coalescing long and short seqs causing hotspots.

anna: yes — tried head_prune=0.8 and kv_evict=tail-2. Performance improved (p99 down ~20%) but Qwen lost some NE task accuracy. We need a per-model safe band rather than global config.

ben: Can you paste the minimal repro prompt and the perplexity snippets so we can run a bisect on head dims?

anna: Minimal prompt used for repro (shortened):
"In 2042, the observatory located at the volcanic plateau recorded a time-lapse of the northern aurora..." (long narrative to stress long-context).
Perplexity diff sample:
```
Mixtral NTK: logprob -12.3, ppl 18.2
Mixtral linear: logprob -11.1, ppl 16.0
```

eva: Suggestion: add a head-entropy metric into kernel routing. If head-entropy drops below threshold (i.e., heads collapse) prefer the linear kernel to avoid splitting.

maya: :thumbsup: I can add instrumentation for head_entropy. Where should I push the patch?

anna: Pushed branch -> github.com/redwood/runtime/rope-headsplit-bisect (PR #1223). It introduces head_entropy telemetry and a fallback to linear if head_entropy > 0.6 for a given head group. Running canary on dedicated pool now.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary deploy queued to pool-r5d-x3 (tag: rope-headsplit-bisect), ETA ~8m.

devon: If canary passes, plan a 10% traffic ramp and enable kv_eviction=aggressive only for Mixtral model instances. Also add a small A/B to compare linear vs NTK on 5k/10k prompt sets.

maya: I'll run the 5k/10k eval suite and post results to the PR.

ben: One more ask: add a kernel tie-breaker that prefers the kernel with smaller L2 working set if observed SM util < 50% to avoid memory-bound splits.

anna: Agreed. Next steps in PR: 1) add head_entropy to kernel routing; 2) add tie-breaker heuristics; 3) enable Mixtral-specific kv eviction policy; 4) run A/B across our long-context eval set. Will update with canary perf numbers once available. Thanks all.
